result.topic_en: Euler shows how timing the immersion and emersion of the Moon in a total lunar eclipse, together with the beginning and end, lets one find the Moon's node relative to the shadow centre and then correct the inclination of the lunar orbit.
result.transcription:
372 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA.

ut ex his observationibus solis locus nodi exacte definiri nequeat. Hancobrem in subsidi[?]... debent aliae observationes, veluti si in eclipsi totali, praeter initium et finem ejus, quoque et emersio observetur. Si enim tempus ab initio eclipsis ad finem elapsum sit $= h$ hor[?]..., semidiameter apparens umbrae $= \alpha$, ac semidiameter lunae apparens $= \beta$, erit $f$ ...[?] in immersione autem et emersione erit arcus $SL = sl = \alpha - \beta$, qui ponatur $= F$; tempus ab[?] immersione ad emersionem elapsum sit $= H$ horarum. Quodsi ergo ponatur $\frac{1}{2}H(n$[?]...
$\frac{1}{2}H(m+k) = B$, manente $\frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x \,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\rho}{g(n-m)} = c$, reperietur simili modo
$$\cos(2x - A - B - c) = \frac{\cos F - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(A-B+c)}{\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\rho}.$$
§ 19. Si jam aequatio prius inventa
$$\cos(2x - a - b - c) = \frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(a-b+c)}{\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\rho}$$
per istam dividatur, reperietur
$$\frac{\cos(2x-a-b-c)}{\cos(2x-A-B-c)} = \frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(a-b+c)}{\cos F - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(A-B+c)},$$
in quam valor $\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\rho$ non amplius ingreditur. Etsi autem in ea etiamnunc terminus $\cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho$ ...[?]
tamen levis incertitudo in angulo $\rho$, cum ipse angulus sit valde parvus, valorem termini $\cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho$[?]
non sensibiliter afficit, atque errores hinc oriundi in numeratore et denominatore fere se mutuo[?]
compensabunt. Aequatio autem inventa resolvetur in sequentem
$$\frac{\cos(a+b+c) + \sin(a+b+c)\,\mathrm{tang}\,2x}{\cos(A+B+c) + \sin(A+B+c)\,\mathrm{tang}\,2x} = \frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(a-b+c)}{\cos F - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(A-B+c)}$$
ex qua valor $\mathrm{tang}\,2x$, ac proinde ipse arcus $☊\sigma$, quo nodus a loco centri umbrae medio eclipsis[?]
momento distat, assignari poterit. Sit enim brevitatis gratia
$$\frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(a-b+c)}{\cos F - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(A-B+c)} = d$$
erit $\mathrm{tang}\,2x = \frac{-\cos(a+b+c) + d\cos(A+B+c)}{-d\sin(A+B+c) + \sin(a+b+c)}$.

§ 20. Invento loco nodi seu distantia $☊\sigma = x$, existente $\sigma$ loco centri umbrae momento medio[?]
eclipsis, inde porro inclinatio orbitae lunae ad eclipticam, seu angulus $☊ = \rho$, accuratius defini[?]...
poterit. Cum enim iste angulus $\rho$ jam tam prope sit cognitus, ut terminus $\cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho$ minime a veri[?]...
tate discrepet, erit
$$\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\rho = \frac{\cos f - \cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho\cos(a-b+c)}{\cos(2x-a-b-c)}, \text{ seu } \cos\rho = \frac{\cos f - \cos(x-a-c)\cos(x-b)}{\sin(x-a-c)\sin(x-b)}$$
sive etiam $\sin^2\frac{1}{2}\rho = \frac{\cos(a-b+c) - \cos f}{2\sin(x-a-c)\sin(x-b)} = \frac{\cos(a-b+c)-\cos f}{\cos(a-b+c) - \cos(2x-a-b-c)} = \frac{\sin\left(\frac{f+a-b+c}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{f-a+b-c}{2}\right)}{\sin(x-a-c)\sin(x-b)}$[?]

items.quote: ut ex his observationibus solis locus nodi exacte definiri nequeat
items.english: so that from these observations alone the place of the node cannot be exactly determined

items.quote: Hancobrem in subsidi[?]... debent aliae observationes, veluti si in eclipsi totali, praeter initium et finem ejus, quoque et emersio observetur.
items.english: Therefore other observations must be brought in to help, for example if in a total eclipse the emersion is also observed, besides its beginning and end.

items.quote:
tamen levis incertitudo in angulo $\rho$, cum ipse angulus sit valde parvus, valorem termini $\cos^2\frac{1}{2}\rho$[?]
non sensibiliter afficit, atque errores hinc oriundi in numeratore et denominatore fere se mutuo[?]
compensabunt.
items.english: yet a slight uncertainty in the angle rho, since the angle itself is very small, does not sensibly affect the value of the term cos^2(rho/2), and the errors arising from it in numerator and denominator will nearly compensate each other.

items.quote:
ex qua valor $\mathrm{tang}\,2x$, ac proinde ipse arcus $☊\sigma$, quo nodus a loco centri umbrae medio eclipsis[?]
momento distat, assignari poterit.
items.english: from which the value of tan 2x, and hence the arc from node to sigma, by which the node is distant from the place of the shadow's centre at the middle moment of the eclipse, can be assigned.

items.quote:
inde porro inclinatio orbitae lunae ad eclipticam, seu angulus $☊ = \rho$, accuratius defini[?]...
poterit.
items.english: from this, further, the inclination of the lunar orbit to the ecliptic, that is the angle at the node = rho, can be determined more accurately.
